To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the errors introduced by errors in the intrinsic parameters can be characterized by the projection matrix of the camera; (2) the errors in the intrinsic parameter estimates are propagated to errors in the reconstructed image; (3) the error in the reconstructed image can be expressed in terms of the error in the intrinsic parameters; and (4) the error in intrinsic parameters can be recovered from the error in the image.
the errors in intrinsic camera parameters can be recovered by a process that involves projecting rectilinear images onto a cylindrical surface and compositing those images.

(1) the correct focal length can always be recovered, and (2) the recovered focal length is independent of the number of original images, their resolution, and the number of pixels in the panoramic image.
